doc.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Writing children's books with his brother Christopher
summary: His brother Christopher does the research and he writes the story, with his own visits to battlefields and museums.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I brought one of the many With Every Drop of Blood book you wrote with your brother Christopher. And I wonder sometimes if you’re going to write about the Civil War where does your research come from? Where do you go to try to write authentic battle scenes and those kinds of specific things?

Well the story is this. Most of my children’s books I write by myself but I did I think eight with my brother. My brother recently retired but he was an American historian at the University of Connecticut and he was the State Historian for Connecticut, a very good historian. And so we started writing together and the first book we had was called My Brother Sam is Dead and it was an enormous success, it won all the prizes and everything. And still sells a hundred thousand copies a year, which is a lot less money than you think because it’s an inexpensive paperback, but still. So he does the research. And he comes to me with a pile of material and says “here it is.” And with a general story outline, a very brief story outline that’s based on the historical events. But then I generally do some research and I know for this book, a Civil War book, I went down to Gettysburg obviously, and I went to some of the other battle areas to look at those and I went to whatever museums there were that seemed appropriate. Because you want to get a look at the uniforms, you want to get a look at the swords, at the rifles, you want to get a look at the cannons, you want to take pictures whatever you do. You want to get a look at Gettysburg, you want to see what that looks like. You want to see what those hills are and the valley in between and over here you had the north and over here you had Lee with his bunch, and so you want to do that. But the bulk of the research is done by my brother, and then I take it and write a story about it. So that’s how that works.
